due_when.clears_when: (a) A durable register exists in which every operator-owed item carries an OWNER-CLASS (genuinely-human: secret origination / physical-or-broker / judgement — vs defaulted-to-human: a wire exists or could) and an age; (b) an item aging past a stated threshold ESCALATES rather than being re-listed, and the escalation is measured not asserted; (c) every defaulted-to-human item is either automated or carries a recorded reason it cannot be, with the anti-pattern named — 'one remediation attempt failed' is not sufficient on its own, because the tested-pure-function remedy exists and has a precedent in this repo; (d) ⚠️ THE STANDING PART: a check that FAILS when an item has been carried across N sessions without a state change. Without (d) this closes and silently regresses, which is the same failure the register exists to prevent. Closing on 'a register was created' alone is NOT sufficient — the register must be shown to have MOVED an item at least once.
